edge: Verify complete recursive coverage of a multidimensional array.
negative: Leave at least one array element unmatched.
positive: Cover selected elements explicitly and all remaining elements with default or type keys.

edge: Combine explicit index, type, and default keys to test precedence.
negative: Use a default value that is neither directly applicable nor recursively applicable to an unmatched target.
positive: Set all unmatched scalar elements with a castable default and recursively default nested arrays or structures.

edge: Use signed and unsigned element types.
notes: Size warnings for valid contextual conversions are not required and must not be the oracle.
positive: Initialize bit and int arrays from differently sized literal pattern items and verify per-element conversion.

edge: Contrast with unpacked concatenation flattening of that same array item.
negative: Use an array-valued item where a scalar element type is required.
positive: Use pattern items each having exactly the target element type.

edge: Mix index keys with type and default keys.
negative: Use a value not castable to the indexed element type.
positive: Set selected array indices with values castable to each element type.

edge: Use distinct constant expressions that evaluate to the same index.
negative: Repeat an index key in one pattern.
positive: Specify each keyed index once.

edge: Nest one replication per dimension.
negative: Use a replication count that does not cover the represented dimension.
positive: Use one replication for a one-dimensional array and nested replications for each dimension of a multidimensional array.

edge: Exercise braces whose meaning is resolved by the assignment target.
negative: Use the wrong element count or brace dimensionality.
positive: Initialize a multidimensional array with matching element count and nested braces.

edge: Provide multiple matching type keys and observe the last value.
negative: Supply a matched type-key value not castable to the element type.
positive: Use type keys across an array of structures and a multidimensional array, with an index key taking precedence.

edge: Use unsized operands whose expression sizing interacts with target context.
positive: Assign a context-determined expression to targets of different widths and compare results.

edge: Use an assignment pattern as the left side with a typed right side.
negative: Use an assignment pattern where neither side supplies a self-determined type.
positive: Assign a pattern to a typed structure or array so the target determines member correspondence and types.

edge: Select fields with different widths or signedness in one pattern.
positive: Use a keyed nondefault assignment-pattern item whose expression needs the selected field's type context.

edge: Use a parameter identifier as the pattern-expression type.
negative: Use an unsupported key form or omit required apostrophe/braces.
positive: Parse positional, keyed, default, type-keyed, replicated, and explicitly typed pattern forms.

edge: Use a fractional time-unit literal on a continuous assignment.
positive: Use explicit ns delays before a blocking assignment, on its right-hand side, on a nonblocking assignment, and on a continuous assignment.

edge: Truncate a negative signed value far enough to change the result's sign.

positive: Assign wider signed and unsigned vectors to narrower targets and verify the least-significant target-width bits remain.

edge: Include unknown bits at the sign position.
positive: Assign narrow positive and negative signed values and a narrow unsigned value to wider targets.

edge: Contrast assignment context with a self-determined expression context.
positive: Use a context-sensitive expression in equivalent continuous and procedural assignments and observe target-context conversion.

edge: Assign a whole composite value of the nettype.
negative: Continuously assign to a member, bit-select, or part-select within its data type.
positive: Continuously assign a whole atomic user-defined nettype net.

edge: Exercise arithmetic, bitwise, logical-shift, and arithmetic-shift compound assignments.
negative: Use a non-grammar assignment operator or omit the required right-hand expression.
positive: Parse ordinary blocking, compound, dynamic-array new, class new, and increment/decrement assignment forms.

edge: Repeat with a class handle or virtual-interface reference.

positive: Change an array index across an intra-assignment delay and observe selection at the specified timing-control time.

edge: Join the branches after their independently timed effects.
positive: Place a delayed blocking assignment in one fork branch and observe another branch proceed independently.

edge: Use an intra-assignment delay and verify the following sequential statement waits for completion.

negative: Specify charge strength on a wire declaration.

edge: Use replication with a constant count and members.

edge: Specify distinct rise, fall, and turn-off delays.

positive: Alias two wire nets of equal width.

positive: Compile a legal alias and continue elaboration.

negative: Attempt a second declaration of the same net with another declaration assignment.
positive: Give one declaration assignment to a net.

negative: Omit the right-hand expression or use a non-variable target.
positive: Parse nonblocking assignments with no timing control, a delay, and an event control.

edge: Repeat with a class handle or virtual-interface reference.

positive: Schedule an indexed nonblocking assignment and change the index before update; observe the originally evaluated target update.

edge: Contrast static and automatic lifetime declarations in otherwise identical procedures.

positive: Use nonblocking assignment on a static variable.

edge: Contrast with a fixed-size array element target.

positive: Use blocking assignment on a dynamic-array element.

negative: Place one in a module, interface, or program declaration port expression.
positive: Use an assignment-pattern expression in an ordinary typed assignment.

edge: Use members with equal widths but differing signedness where assignment compatible.
negative: Use a non-bit-stream member, incompatible type, or differing bit count.
positive: Deconstruct into same-width compatible bit-stream members.

negative: Use keyed notation in an untyped pattern target.
positive: Deconstruct an array with a positional pattern target.

edge: Exercise module, interface, and program ports.

positive: Initialize arrays and structures with positional assignment patterns and destructure an array with a positional pattern target.

positive: Procedurally assign the whole variable.

edge: A later procedural assignment replaces the retained value.

edge: Prevent execution from reaching an assignment with a false branch, then trigger it through an event control.

positive: Parse each assign/deassign and force/release grammar form with its permitted target category.

edge: Use a function call whose argument changes in the forced expression.

edge: Use a runtime index.
positive: Procedurally assign a selected array element.

edge: Select a boundary slice.

edge: Use nested concatenations.
negative: Include an illegal target in the concatenation.
positive: Assign procedurally to a concatenation of variable selects.

edge: Select boundary words.
positive: Procedurally assign one word of a memory.

edge: Use a variable index for a bit-select.
positive: Assign to bit-, part-, and slice-selects of a packed variable.

negative: Use a net as a procedural-assignment target.

edge: Exercise assignment compatibility with aggregate targets.
negative: Assign an expression disallowed by the target variable type.
positive: Assign a type-compatible expression to a variable.
